mainTopic: נזיר שמשון and נזיר עולם: whose view the משנה follows, the sources for each, and the meaning of ״לַה׳״
overview: The משנה ends by saying that a נזיר שמשון who becomes טמא does not bring a קרבן טומאה. The גמרא infers that the נזירות itself still takes effect, and asks whose view this is. רבי יהודה lets a נזיר שמשון become טמא even לכתחילה, and רבי שמעון says such a vow does nothing at all. The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי יהודה. The words 'אם נטמא' were only copied from the line about נזיר עולם. Next it asks whether רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון argue like רבי יעקב and רבי יוסי about 'הרי עלי כבכור'. It rejects that link and explains how each side reads the word ״לַה׳״. It then shows that ״לַה׳״ by נזיר means 'for the sake of Heaven', through the story of שמעון הצדיק and the young shepherd. It explains that שמשון's נזירות came from a מלאך, and that we know he became טמא from the dead only through tradition. Finally, רבי teaches that אבשלום was a נזיר עולם who cut his hair once a year.

steps.title: The משנה's last ruling: no impurity offering
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its ruling about a נזיר שמשון: if he becomes טמא, he does not bring a קרבן טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he does not bring an offering for impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the last words of the משנה about a נזיר שמשון. If such a person becomes טמא from a dead body, he does not bring the usual impurity offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular נזיר who becomes טמא from a dead body must bring a קרבן טומאה and start his נזירות over. The משנה says a נזיר שמשון is different on this point. The rest of this section is built on these words.

keyTerms.meaning: The offering a נזיר brings after becoming impure from a dead body
A person who takes a vow to be a נזיר like שמשון

phrases.english: And he does not bring the offering for impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה quoted earlier on the דף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נזיר שמשון who becomes טמא does not bring a קרבן טומאה.

steps.title: Inference: only the offering is skipped, but the נזירות still applies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the משנה closely. Only the offering is missing, so the נזירות itself, including the ban on becoming טמא, is still in force.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is only the offering that he does not bring. But the נזירות does take hold of him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from the exact wording of the משנה. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says that he skips the offering. That implies the נזירות itself really takes effect on him. Read together with the words 'אם נטמא', it at first sounds like he is forbidden to become טמא לכתחילה; step 6 will revisit that.

keyTerms.meaning: The status and rules of being a נזיר

steps.confusionAlert: The inference here only shows that the נזירות really takes effect. The words 'אם נטמא' seem to forbid becoming טמא לכתחילה, but step 6 concludes the משנה follows רבי יהודה, who allows a נזיר שמשון to become טמא even לכתחילה.

phrases.english: It is the offering that he does not bring,
but the naziriteship does take effect on him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the wording of the משנה in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נזיר שמשון is a real נזיר; only the קרבן טומאה is skipped.

steps.title: Whose view is the משנה? Neither רבי יהודה nor רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא the משנה follows. It claims the משנה matches neither רבי יהודה nor רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is the משנה? It is not רבי יהודה, and it is not רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who wrote this משנה and immediately says it does not fit either of two known views. This sets up a ברייתא and then a full explanation of the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the גמרא knows the משנה holds two things (no offering, but real נזירות), it looks for a תנא who holds both. The claim that no known תנא fits turns the question into a challenge.

phrases.english: Whose opinion is the mishna?

phrases.aramaic: לָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וְלָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.
phrases.english: Not Rabbi Yehuda, and not Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the inference of step 2 to ask which תנא the משנה follows.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a נזיר שמשון is a real נזיר but brings no קרבן טומאה?

steps.title: The ברייתא: רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון on נזיר שמשון
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives both views. רבי יהודה says a נזיר שמשון may become טמא from the dead. רבי שמעון says saying 'נזיר שמשון' does nothing at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says a נזיר שמשון may become impure from the dead, because we find that שמשון became impure. רבי שמעון says one who says 'נזיר שמשון' has said nothing, because we never find that שמשון said a vow of נזירות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show what רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון each hold. This is the source for its claim that the משנה fits neither of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תנאים learn from the real שמשון. רבי יהודה points to the fact that שמשון became טמא, so his kind of נזיר may become טמא. רבי שמעון points to the fact that שמשון never made a vow, so a vow to be like him is empty.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
To become impure from dead bodies
He has said nothing (his words have no legal effect)

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
A Samson-nazirite is permitted to become impure from the dead,
since we find with Samson that he became impure.
Rabbi Shimon says:
One who says "a Samson-nazirite" has not said anything,
since we do not find with Samson
that naziriteship came out of his mouth.
phrases.notes: שמשון never made a vow himself; he became a נזיר through the angel's words to his mother (שופטים 13:5).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the ברייתא behind the claim in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the משנה matches neither רבי יהודה nor רבי שמעון.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא giving the views of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון on נזיר שמשון.

steps.title: Why the משנה fits neither תנא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the problem. רבי יהודה allows becoming טמא even לכתחילה, but the משנה says 'if he became טמא'. רבי שמעון says the נזירות does not take effect at all, but the משנה treats it as real.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose is it? If רבי יהודה, he said it is allowed even לכתחילה, yet the משנה says 'if he became impure.' If רבי שמעון, he said נזירות does not take effect on him at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly why each תנא clashes with the משנה. Each one disagrees with a different half of what the משנה holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'אם נטמא' (if he became impure) imply that becoming טמא is forbidden לכתחילה, which goes against רבי יהודה. The משנה also treats this person as a real נזיר, which goes against רבי שמעון. So the משנה still has no matching author.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start, as a first choice
If he became impure (after the fact)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה holds two things: he is a real נזיר (against רבי שמעון), and he may not become טמא לכתחילה (against רבי יהודה). So far it matches neither.

phrases.english: Whose is it? If Rabbi Yehuda —
didn't he say even ab initio,
phrases.notes: He means רבי יהודה lets this נזיר become impure from the dead even from the start.

phrases.english: and the mishna teaches "if he became impure."
If Rabbi Shimon —

phrases.aramaic: הָאָמַר לָא חָיְילָא עֲלֵיהּ נְזִירוּת כְּלָל!
phrases.english: didn't he say naziriteship does not take effect on him at all!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא in step 4 to the משנה and shows why neither view fits.
steps.kashyaTarget: Assigning the משנה to either רבי יהודה or רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording 'אם נטמא' means becoming טמא is forbidden לכתחילה, against רבי יהודה. Treating the person as a real נזיר goes against רבי שמעון, who says the vow does nothing.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי יהודה; the wording just copies the נזיר עולם line
steps.stepSummary: The משנה really follows רבי יהודה. It says 'if he became טמא' only because it used that same phrase for נזיר עולם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the משנה is רבי יהודה. Since the משנה said 'if he became טמא' about a נזיר עולם, it used the same words, 'if he became טמא', about a נזיר שמשון too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem from step 5. The משנה follows רבי יהודה, and the words 'if he became טמא' are just copied from the line about נזיר עולם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5 the phrase 'if he became טמא' sounded like becoming טמא was forbidden, which clashes with רבי יהודה. The answer is that the phrase is not precise for נזיר שמשון. It was written to keep the same style as the נזיר עולם line, where becoming טמא really is forbidden. So a נזיר שמשון may become טמא even לכתחילה, as רבי יהודה says.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually; the גמרא keeps its original position
Since / because of; the wording was carried over from another case
A permanent נזיר, who is forbidden to become טמא

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'if he became טמא' as proof that a נזיר שמשון is forbidden to become טמא. The גמרא says the phrase was only borrowed from the נזיר עולם line.

phrases.english: Really, it is רבי יהודה,
and since it teaches regarding a permanent נזיר
"if he became impure,"
it also taught regarding a נזיר שמשון
"if he became impure."
phrases.notes: For a נזיר שמשון this phrase isn't exact. He may become טמא even לכתחילה.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא, וְאַיְּידֵי דְּקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 5 by matching the משנה to רבי יהודה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Stylistic wording (איידי): the phrase is carried over from a parallel case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'If he became טמא' shows that becoming טמא is forbidden, so the משנה can't be רבי יהודה
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase is borrowed from the נזיר עולם line, so the משנה fits רבי יהודה

steps.title: Suggesting the argument matches the case of 'like a firstborn'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון argue about the same thing as רבי יעקב and רבי יוסי in the case of 'הרי עלי כבכור'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say they argue about the same thing these תנאים argue about? We learned: if someone says 'this is upon me like a בכור', רבי יעקב forbids it and רבי יוסי permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question: maybe the argument about נזיר שמשון is really an older argument. It quotes a case about 'like a בכור' to set up the comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור is holy from birth, not because someone made a vow on it. Someone who says 'this object is like a בכור to me' is tying his vow to something that was never vowed. רבי יעקב says the vow works; רבי יוסי says it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? It introduces a suggestion
A firstborn animal, holy from birth

phrases.english: Shall we say they disagree in the dispute of these תנאים,
as we learned: "It is upon me like a firstborn,"
phrases.notes: He means: this object is forbidden to me the way a בכור animal is forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אוֹסֵר, וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי מַתִּיר.
phrases.english: רבי יעקב forbids, and רבי יוסי permits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the משנה, the גמרא looks for the root of the רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון argument
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the argument about נזיר שמשון the same as the argument about 'like a בכור'?

steps.title: Matching each side to רבי יעקב and רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The proposal: רבי יהודה holds like רבי יעקב (no need for a vowed item), and רבי שמעון holds like רבי יוסי (a vowed item is required).
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it so that רבי יהודה holds like רבי יעקב, who says we don't need a vowed item? And רבי שמעון holds like רבי יוסי, who says we do need a vowed item?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out its suggestion and pairs each תנא with one side of the בכור argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like a בכור, שמשון's נזירות did not come from a vow; it came from an angel's command. If a vow does not have to point to a vowed item, then 'I am like שמשון' works, as רבי יהודה says. If it must point to one, then saying it does nothing, as רבי שמעון says.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it that...? It presses a suggested reading
An item that became forbidden through a vow

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב,
phrases.english: Isn't it that רבי יהודה holds like רבי יעקב,
who said: we do not require an item forbidden by a vow,
phrases.notes: In other words, you can tie your vow to something that is holy by its own nature, like a בכור.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: and רבי שמעון holds like רבי יוסי,
who said: we do require an item forbidden by a vow?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לָאו, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the suggestion from step 7 by pairing the opinions
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון argue about whether a vow needs a דבר הנידר
steps.raayaSupportSource: The argument between רבי יעקב and רבי יוסי about 'הרי עלי כבכור'

steps.title: Everyone requires a vowed item; a בכור is a special case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the pairing. Everyone agrees a vowed item is needed, and רבי יעקב makes an exception for a בכור because the פסוק 'לה׳' includes it.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees we need a vowed item. A בכור is different, because the פסוק says 'to ה׳', which comes to include the בכור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion. The בכור argument does not prove anything about נזיר שמשון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both רבי יעקב and רבי יוסי agree that a vow must point to a vowed item. רבי יעקב permits 'like a בכור' only because a פסוק adds the בכור to this rule. So the argument of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון cannot be explained this way.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה follows רבי יהודה. The argument of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון is not the same as the בכור argument, because everyone agrees a vowed item is needed and the בכור is a special case from a פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא בָּעִינַן דָּבָר הַנִּידָּר,
phrases.english: No, everyone agrees we require an item forbidden by a vow,
but it is different regarding a firstborn,
for it is written about it: "to ה׳"
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק about vows, במדבר ל:ג.

phrases.english: to include the firstborn.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא בָּעִינַן דָּבָר הַנִּידָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the pairing proposed in steps 7 and 8
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects tying the נזיר שמשון argument to the בכור argument
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יעקב's ruling comes from a special פסוק about בכור, not from a general rule that a vowed item isn't needed

steps.title: רבי יוסי uses the word ״לַה׳״ for something else
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי explains why he does not learn בכור from 'לה׳': he needs that word to include חטאת and אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי would answer you: that word 'לה׳' is needed to include a חטאת and an אשם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי יוסי would defend himself. He agrees that 'לה׳' includes something, but he says it includes חטאת and אשם, not בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9 רבי יעקב used 'לה׳' to include a בכור. רבי יוסי does not deny that the word includes something extra. He just moves it to different קרבנות, so his rule (a vowed item is needed) still holds for בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: 'To the Lord', the word in the פסוק that each side uses to include something extra
He needs it (for a different purpose)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei would say to you:
That word 'to the Lord,' he needs it
phrases.notes: This is the same word רבי יעקב used in step 9 to include a בכור.

phrases.english: to include a sin-offering and a guilt-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יוסי's side after step 9 explained רבי יעקב's use of 'לה׳'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the extra word in the פסוק to a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since 'לה׳' includes something, maybe it must include בכור, and רבי יוסי should agree.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי uses 'לה׳' for חטאת and אשם, so a בכור is still not included.

steps.title: Why include sin- and guilt-offerings rather than a firstborn?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what reason there is to include חטאת and אשם and leave out בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what made you decide to include חטאת and אשם and to leave out the בכור?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks רבי יוסי to explain his choice. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a word includes something extra, we need a reason to pick one thing over another. The גמרא wants the logic that makes חטאת and אשם a better fit than בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: And what did you see? (What is your reason?)
A firstborn male animal, which is holy from birth

phrases.english: And what did you see
to include a sin-offering and a guilt-offering
and to exclude the firstborn?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the choice רבי יוסי made in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for including חטאת and אשם in 'לה׳' and leaving out בכור.

steps.title: Sin- and guilt-offerings become holy by a person's act, a firstborn does not
steps.stepSummary: חטאת and אשם get their holiness when a person sets them aside, which is like a vow. A בכור does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: I include חטאת and אשם, because a person gives them their holiness with a vow-like act. I leave out the בכור, because a person does not give it holiness with a vow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. חטאת and אשם are like vowed items, so they are included; בכור is not, so it is left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person cannot promise to bring a חטאת or אשם, but when he sets aside a specific animal for one, that act works like a vow. A בכור becomes holy by itself at birth, with no act by a person. That is why only חטאת and אשם fit רבי יוסי's rule that a vowed item is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: One gives them holiness through a vow (or a vow-like act)

phrases.english: I include a sin-offering and a guilt-offering
since one gives them their holiness through a vow,
phrases.notes: Setting aside a specific animal to be a חטאת or אשם counts like making a vow on it.

phrases.english: and I exclude the firstborn
since one does not give it holiness through a vow.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְרַבֶּה אֲנִי חַטָּאת וְאָשָׁם שֶׁכֵּן מַתְפִּיסָן בְּנֶדֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חטאת and אשם become holy through a person's vow-like act; a בכור does not, so only they fit.

steps.title: רבי יעקב: a firstborn is also made holy by a person
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב argues that a בכור also gets holiness from a person, bringing a ברייתא that there is a מצוה to consecrate it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יעקב would answer you: a בכור is also made holy through a vow. As it was taught in a ברייתא: the חכמים of רבי's house said: How do we know that when a בכור is born in a person's herd, there is a מצוה for him to consecrate it? Because the פסוק says, 'the male you shall sanctify.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי יעקב would push back on רבי יוסי's distinction. He brings a ברייתא to prove that a person does consecrate a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי said a בכור is different because no person makes it holy. רבי יעקב points to a ברייתא: there is a מצוה to say the words that consecrate a בכור. So a בכור is also made holy by a person, just like חטאת and אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (in a ברייתא)
Those of the house of our רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא)
To consecrate it, to declare it holy
'The male you shall sanctify', the פסוק about a בכור

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yaakov would say to you:
A firstborn too is given holiness through a vow.
As it was taught: those of the house of our Rebbi said:
phrases.notes: 'Our רבי' means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לְנוֹלַד לוֹ בְּכוֹר בְּתוֹךְ עֶדְרוֹ
phrases.english: From where do we know that when a firstborn is born in his herd
there is a מצוה on him to consecrate it?
As it says: 'The male you shall sanctify.'
phrases.notes: דברים 15:19

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר לָךְ בְּכוֹר נָמֵי מַתְפִּיסוֹ בְּנֶדֶר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the distinction given in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 12 that a בכור is not made holy through a vow.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says there is a מצוה to consecrate a בכור, so a person does give it holiness, just like חטאת and אשם.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the house of רבי, based on 'הַזָּכָר תַּקְדִּישׁ'.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: a firstborn is holy even without being consecrated
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי answers that even though there is a מצוה to consecrate a בכור, it is holy by itself even if the owner never does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי would answer you: Fine, there is a מצוה to consecrate it. But if he does not consecrate it, is it not holy anyway?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי pushes away רבי יעקב's proof. The מצוה to consecrate a בכור does not make the person the source of its holiness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only shows there is a מצוה to say the words. But a בכור is holy from birth whether or not the owner says anything. So its holiness does not come from a vow, and רבי יוסי's distinction between בכור and חטאת/אשם still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not holy? (Of course it is holy)

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree that 'לה׳' includes something extra. רבי יעקב says it includes בכור; רבי יוסי says it includes חטאת and אשם, because a בכור is holy by itself from birth and not through a person's vow.
steps.confusionAlert: The מצוה to consecrate a בכור is real, but it does not create the holiness. The בכור is already holy at birth; saying the words is an extra מצוה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei would say to you:
Granted that there is a מצוה to consecrate it,
if he does not consecrate it,
is it not holy?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אָמַר לָךְ נְהִי דְּמִצְוָה לְהַקְדִּישׁוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the ברייתא brought in step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי יעקב's proof that a בכור is made holy through a vow.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A מצוה to consecrate does not mean the holiness depends on it, since a בכור is holy from birth even without consecration.

steps.title: The word ״לַה׳״ also appears by נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון: the פסוק about נזיר also says ״לַה׳״, so why not learn from it that one can become a נזיר like שמשון?
steps.simpleTranslation: By נזיר too, doesn't the פסוק say 'to ה׳'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge. The same word ״לַה׳״ that was used to learn about vows also appears in the פסוק about נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, ״לַה׳״ taught that a person can make a vow by linking it to something whose holiness did not come from a vow. If so, ״לַה׳״ by נזיר should teach that a person can accept a נזירות like שמשון's, even though שמשון never vowed. So why does רבי שמעון say such a person is not a נזיר?

keyTerms.meaning: with regard to, in the case of
a person who vows to stay away from wine, haircuts and טומאת מת

phrases.english: With regard to a nazirite as well,
isn't it written "to the Lord"!
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:2

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the ״לַה׳״ lesson from the vow discussion and applies it to נזיר, challenging רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's ruling that one who says 'I am like שמשון' is not a נזיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ״לַה׳״ by vows includes things whose holiness did not come from a vow, the same word by נזיר should include שמשון's נזירות, which did not come from a vow.

steps.title: The word is needed for a teaching of שמעון הצדיק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that ״לַה׳״ by נזיר is needed for a different lesson. It begins a ברייתא in which שמעון הצדיק describes a handsome young man who came to him as a נזיר טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word is needed for what a ברייתא teaches. שמעון הצדיק said: I never ate the אשם of a נזיר טמא, except for one man from the South. He had beautiful eyes and a fine face, and his hair was arranged in curls. I asked him: My son, why did you choose to destroy this beautiful hair?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ״לַה׳״ is already used for something else, and it starts telling a story from a ברייתא to show what that is. This step sets up the story; the lesson comes at the end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A word can only teach one lesson, so if ״לַה׳״ is busy teaching something else, it cannot teach about שמשון. The story shows a one-time exception: the only נזיר טמא whose אשם שמעון הצדיק agreed to eat. His question sets up the young man's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: he needs it (for a different lesson)
as was taught in a ברייתא
a כהן גדול in the early days of the second בית המקדש
the guilt-offering a נזיר brings after becoming impure

steps.confusionAlert: This story is not a side trip. It is the גמרא's answer: it shows that ״לַה׳״ by נזיר is used for 'for the sake of Heaven.'

phrases.english: That is needed by him
for that which is taught in a ברייתא:
Shimon HaTzaddik said:
In all my days I never ate
the guilt-offering of an impure nazirite,
except for one man
who came to me from the South,
with beautiful eyes and a fine appearance,
and his locks were arranged in curls.
I said to him: My son,
what did you see to destroy
this beautiful hair?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15 by saying the word ״לַה׳״ is already used for another lesson.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Word is used for a different lesson (מיבעי ליה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״לַה׳״ by נזיר is free to include a נזירות that did not come from a vow, like שמשון's.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״לַה׳״ by נזיר is needed for the lesson of the ברייתא about vowing for the sake of Heaven.

steps.title: The young man explains why he became a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The young man tells שמעון הצדיק that he saw his reflection, felt his יצר הרע pull him toward pride, and swore to shave his hair for the sake of Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: I was a shepherd for my father in my town. I went to draw water from the spring and looked at my reflection. My יצר quickly rose against me and tried to drive me out of the world. I said to it: Empty one! Why are you proud in a world that is not yours, when you will end up as maggots and worms? I swear by the Temple service that I will shave you for the sake of Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The young man answers שמעון הצדיק's question. He explains that he became a נזיר to fight his own pride.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seeing his good looks made his יצר הרע push him toward vanity, which could ruin him. He answered his יצר by reminding it that the body ends up in the grave. He took on נזירות so he would have to shave his beautiful hair, purely to serve ה׳. This pure reason is what the next step praises.

keyTerms.meaning: to drive me out of the world (to ruin me)
'by the Temple service', a form of oath

phrases.english: He said to me:
I was a shepherd for my father in my town,
and I went to draw water from the spring,
and I looked at my reflection,
and my inclination quickly rose against me,
and sought to drive me from the world.
I said to it: Empty one!
phrases.notes: He is talking to his own יצר הרע here, not to a person.

phrases.english: For what reason are you proud
in a world that is not yours,
as your end is to be maggots and worms?
By the Temple service, I will shave you for the sake of Heaven.
phrases.notes: "הָעֲבוֹדָה" is a way of swearing. Shaving his hair means he will become a נזיר.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לִי: רוֹעֶה הָיִיתִי לְאָבִי בְּעִירִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question שמעון הצדיק asked inside the story in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why would this handsome young man become a נזיר and lose his beautiful hair?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He became a נזיר to defeat his pride and to serve ה׳, purely for the sake of Heaven.

steps.title: שמעון הצדיק applies ״לַה׳״ to this נזיר
steps.stepSummary: שמעון הצדיק kisses the young man and says the פסוק ״לְהַזִּיר לַה׳״ is about him. This shows that ״לַה׳״ by נזיר means 'for the sake of Heaven.'
steps.simpleTranslation: I stood up and kissed him on his head. I said to him: May there be more נזירים like you in Israel. About you the פסוק says: 'A man who clearly makes a vow, a נזיר's vow, to separate himself to ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with שמעון הצדיק praising the young man and reading the פסוק about him. This finishes the גמרא's answer to step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words ״לְהַזִּיר לַה׳״ describe a נזירות taken on purely for ה׳, like this young man's. Since ״לַה׳״ by נזיר is used for that lesson, it is not free to teach that one can become a נזיר like שמשון. So רבי שמעון's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: clearly states, makes a special statement

steps.whatToRemember: By נזיר, ״לַה׳״ teaches that the vow should be for the sake of Heaven, like the young shepherd's. Because that word is used up, רבי שמעון cannot learn from it that 'I am like שמשון' makes someone a נזיר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא: a word that seems available for a lesson is shown to be already 'busy' with a different lesson.

phrases.english: I stood and kissed him on his head,
I said to him:
May there be more nazirites like you in Israel;
about you the verse says:
"A man who shall clearly utter
to vow the vow of a nazirite
to separate himself to the Lord."
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:2. This is the same ״לַה׳״ from step 15, here read as 'for the sake of Heaven.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story and links the young man's pure intention to the word ״לַה׳״, completing the answer begun in step 16.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ״לַה׳״ by נזיר means a vow made for the sake of Heaven, so it cannot be used to include a נזירות like שמשון's.

steps.title: Wasn't שמשון called a נזיר in the פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that שמשון's נזירות did not come from a vow, quoting the פסוק that calls him a נזיר from the womb.
steps.simpleTranslation: Was שמשון not a נזיר? The פסוק says: 'For the child shall be a נזיר of God from the womb'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the earlier claim by pointing to a פסוק that clearly calls שמשון a נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא treated שמשון's נזירות as something that did not come from a person's vow. Now it asks: the פסוק calls him 'נזיר אלהים,' so isn't that a vow-based נזירות like any other?

keyTerms.meaning: From the womb, meaning from birth
But isn't it written? It brings a פסוק to challenge a claim

phrases.english: And was Samson not a nazirite?
phrases.notes: He means a נזיר who became one through a vow, like a regular נזיר.

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
"For a nazirite of God shall
the child be from the womb"!
phrases.notes: שופטים 13:5

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the claim that שמשון's נזירות was not from a vow and tests it against a פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that שמשון's נזירות did not come from a vow.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק explicitly calls him a נזיר, so his status looks like ordinary vow-based נזירות.

steps.title: An angel said it, not a person
steps.stepSummary: The words in that פסוק were spoken by the מלאך, so שמשון's נזירות did not come from a human vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it was the angel who said it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the 'נזיר' statement came from a מלאך, not from anyone making a vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular נזיר becomes one by saying words of a vow himself. שמשון never did that. The מלאך announced his status before he was born, so he is still a נזיר, just not one created by a vow.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying שמשון was not a נזיר at all. He was a נזיר, but his נזירות came from the מלאך's announcement, not from a vow.

phrases.english: There it was an angel who said it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק calling שמשון a נזיר shows his status came from a vow.
steps.terutzMaskana: The statement came from a מלאך, so it is not a human vow.

steps.title: Where do we see שמשון became impure from the dead?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that שמשון became טמא from dead bodies and suggests the פסוק about killing a thousand men with a jawbone.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that שמשון became impure from the dead? If you say it is from the פסוק 'With the jawbone of a donkey I struck a thousand men'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how we know that שמשון made himself טמא from the dead, and offers a first possible source. This sets up the next move, which tests that source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular נזיר may not become טמא from a dead body, so the גמרא wants proof that שמשון did. The first idea is that killing a thousand men must have involved contact with their bodies.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know?
If you say; it introduces a suggestion that will be tested

phrases.english: And from where do we know that he became impure from the dead?
If you say it is from what is written:
"With the jawbone of a donkey I struck a thousand men"
phrases.notes: שופטים 15:16

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the source of שמשון's נזירות to the source that he became טמא from the dead.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that שמשון became טמא from dead bodies.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The jawbone פסוק is suggested first but rejected (step 22). The final answer is that it is a received tradition (step 27).

steps.title: Maybe he threw the jawbone without touching them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the jawbone proof: perhaps שמשון threw it at them and never touched the bodies.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps he threw it at them and did not touch them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the first proof by showing the פסוק does not prove any contact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Killing someone with a thrown object does not mean you touched the body. So the jawbone פסוק could fit a שמשון who stayed טהור.

phrases.english: Perhaps he threw it at them
and did not touch them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the source suggested in step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The jawbone פסוק as proof of טומאת מת.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Killing by throwing does not require touching the body.

steps.title: A second proof: he took the clothes of thirty men
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new פסוק: שמשון struck thirty men and took their garments, which seems to require touching the bodies.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the proof is from here: 'And he struck thirty men of them and took their garments.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a stronger proof, a פסוק where שמשון took clothes off the men he killed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking clothing off a body requires handling it. If the men were dead, שמשון must have touched dead bodies and become טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, from here; it introduces a new source

phrases.english: Rather, from here:
"And he struck thirty men of them
and took their garments."
phrases.notes: שופטים 14:19

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof of step 22 with a new פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That שמשון became טמא from dead bodies.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שופטים 14:19, where he struck thirty men and took their garments.

steps.title: Maybe he took the clothes first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof: perhaps שמשון stripped the men while they were alive and only then killed them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps he stripped them first and afterward killed them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes a hole in the new proof by suggesting a different order of events.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Touching a living person causes no טומאה. If he took the clothes before killing them, there was no contact with a dead body.

phrases.english: Perhaps he stripped them first
and afterward killed them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof brought in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from the thirty men's garments.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the stripping happened before the killing, he only touched living people.

steps.title: The פסוק's order: first struck, then took
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוק writes 'he struck' before 'he took,' so the killing came first.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'And he struck... and took,' in that order.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the proof by pointing to the order of the words in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists the striking before the taking. That order shows he killed them first and then took their clothes, so he touched dead bodies.

phrases.english: "And he struck... and took" is written.
phrases.notes: The point is the order: striking comes first in the פסוק, taking comes second.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the order of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He may have stripped them before killing them.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק's order shows the killing came first.

steps.title: Maybe they were dying but still alive
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof again: perhaps he only wounded them fatally and took their clothes while they were still alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps he made them into dying people, still alive, and took their clothes then!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that even with the פסוק's order, the proof still does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'He struck' could mean he struck them a deadly blow without them dying yet. A גוסס is still alive, so touching him does not make you טמא from the dead.

keyTerms.meaning: People in the final moments before death, still alive

phrases.english: But perhaps he made them into dying people!
phrases.notes: A גוסס is someone about to die but still alive, so he does not make you טמא like a dead body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Knocks down the proof even after the defense of step 25.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the thirty men's garments as a whole.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'He struck' may mean a fatal wound, with the men still alive when he took their clothes.

steps.title: We know it from a tradition
steps.stepSummary: Since no פסוק proves it, the גמרא concludes that it is a received tradition that שמשון became טמא from the dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we know it as a tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on finding a פסוק and concludes that this fact is known from tradition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both proposed פסוקים could be read without שמשון touching a dead body. So the source is not a פסוק but a tradition passed down.

keyTerms.meaning: We have it as a received tradition

steps.whatToRemember: שמשון's נזירות came from a מלאך, not a vow. The fact that he became טמא from the dead is known from tradition, not from any פסוק.

phrases.english: Rather: we have learned it as a tradition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the search for a source after both proofs were rejected.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: That שמשון became טמא from dead bodies is known through tradition, not from a פסוק.

steps.title: Where is a permanent נזיר written?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source in תנ"ך for the idea of a נזיר עולם.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where is a permanent נזיר written?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new question: where do we find a נזיר עולם in the פסוקים? This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the גמרא was finding sources for שמשון, the נזיר שמשון. Now it turns to the other special kind of נזיר, the נזיר עולם, and asks where that idea is found.

keyTerms.meaning: A permanent נזיר, who stays a נזיר for life but may trim his heavy hair

phrases.english: And a permanent nazirite, where is it written?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the search for a source about שמשון, the גמרא opens a parallel search for נזיר עולם.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק in תנ"ך that shows the existence of a נזיר עולם.

steps.title: אבשלום was a permanent נזיר
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי: אבשלום was a נזיר עולם, as seen from the פסוק about paying his vow in חברון.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי says: אבשלום was a permanent נזיר, as it says: 'And it was at the end of forty years, and אבשלום said to the king: Let me go and pay my vow that I vowed to ה' in חברון.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא: רבי says אבשלום was a נזיר עולם. The proof is the פסוק where אבשלום speaks about a vow he made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says אבשלום had a נדר to ה', and רבי understands this vow as a vow of נזירות. The next step adds that he cut his hair once a year. A regular נזיר may not do that, which marks him as a נזיר עולם.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi says:
phrases.notes: "רבי" with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: Absalom was a permanent nazirite,
as it is said: "And it was at the end of forty years,
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 15:7

phrases.english: and Absalom said to the king:
Please let me go and pay my vow
that I vowed to the Lord, in Hebron."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: אַבְשָׁלוֹם נְזִיר עוֹלָם הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 28 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אבשלום is the example of a נזיר עולם, based on the vow he mentions in שמואל ב 15:7.

steps.title: אבשלום cut his hair once a year
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that אבשלום cut his hair once every twelve months, proven from the פסוק 'at the end of days to days.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And he would cut his hair once every twelve months, as it says: 'And it was at the end of days to days.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and shows how often אבשלום cut his hair: once a year. It proves this from another פסוק about him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר עולם is allowed to lighten his hair when it gets heavy. The פסוק says he cut it 'מִקֵּץ יָמִים לַיָּמִים', and the word ימים here means a full year, so the cutting happened every twelve months.

keyTerms.meaning: From year to year; here ימים means a full year

steps.whatToRemember: רבי teaches that אבשלום was a נזיר עולם, and he cut his heavy hair once every twelve months.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'ימים' as just 'some days.' Here it means a full year, which is how we get twelve months.

phrases.english: And he would cut his hair once every twelve months,
as it is said: "And it was at the end of days to days."
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 14:26. "ימים" here means a year, so "days to days" means once a year.

steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל ב 14:26: 'מִקֵּץ יָמִים לַיָּמִים', read as once a year.
